none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references:
- A. S. Nemirovskii and D. B. Yudin. [Cesari Convergence of the Gradient Method of Approximating Saddle Points of Convex-Concave Functions](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~y328yu/classics/Cesari.pdf). 1978. Complexity: $O(1+G^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)$ fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected objective gap $\le\varepsilon$, using averaged projected iterates on a radius-$R$ ball.
- Daniela Angela Parletta, Andrea Paudice, and Saverio Salzo. [An Improved Analysis of the Clipped Stochastic subGradient Method under Heavy-Tailed Noise](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.00573v2). 2024 preprint; version used: April 2025, v2. Complexity: $O(1+G^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)$ fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected last-iterate objective gap $\le\varepsilon$, with moment order $p=2$, batch size one, base stepsize $R/G$, and base clipping parameter $G$, for $R>0$.
- Prateek Jain, Dheeraj Nagaraj, and Praneeth Netrapalli. [Making the Last Iterate of SGD Information Theoretically Optimal](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.12443v2). 2019, COLT; full analysis: May 2019 preprint, v2. Complexity: $O(1+G^2D^2/\varepsilon^2)$ fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected last-iterate objective gap $\le\varepsilon$, using projected SGD with epochwise decreasing stepsizes; $D$ is the feasible-set diameter.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a real-valued convex function f on a real separable Hilbert space E. A global minimizer xstar exists with ||x0-xstar||≤R. Neither smoothness nor strong convexity is assumed.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Params; spec.admissible, ConvexOn and minimizer-existence clauses.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query x returns grad(ξ,x). Independent samples ξ follow the hidden law M.law. The mean g(x)=Eξ[grad(ξ,x)] belongs to ∂f(x); individual replies need not themselves be subgradients. Only the vector reply is available.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Model; spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible, infinitePi oracle law and mean-subgradient inequality.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform total second-moment bound Eξ||grad(ξ,x)||²≤G² for every x, including integrability. Consequently Eξ||grad(ξ,x)-g(x)||²≤G². Almost-sure boundedness and higher moments are not required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: spec.admissible, squared-norm integrability and second-moment bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is complete, real, and second-countable with its Borel measurable structure. G>0, R≥0, ε>0, x0, and β∈[0,1) are public; f, grad, and the sampling law are hidden. Permitted algorithms are restricted to constantMomentumSgd β γ N x0 for some γ and N. The initial-distance bound and mean-subgradient moment bound imply that f is G-Lipschitz.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Params; Model; spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.allowedAlgorithm, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The E-valued output must have an integrable objective gap f(output)-f(xstar) for a global minimizer xstar, with its expectation at most ε. The successful predicate contains no separate averaging or iterate-selection requirement; the output is constrained through the permitted algorithm family.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[f(output)-f(xstar)]≤ε under the product of the algorithm's randomness and the independent oracle-sample law. Oracle cost is bounded by the supplied deterministic budget for every seed realization.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, product probability measure and per-seed call-count bound.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Convex stochastic subgradient optimization with independent samples, bounded second moments, a known initial-distance bound, and expected objective accuracy is a standard formulation. The permitted momentum family restricts the algorithms used to solve it.
